title: California's immigration-status-neutral Medi-Cal expansion converted formal eligibility into initial care access, while continuity remains conditional
source_unit: California Department of Health Care Services and California Health Care Foundation focus-group study of newly eligible undocumented adults
geography: California; statewide Medi-Cal policy with a qualitative study of nearly 100 undocumented adults

eligibility.value: Full-scope Medi-Cal became available to otherwise eligible adults ages 26 through 49 regardless of immigration status

administrative_route.value: Eligible residents were automatically given the expanded benefits, subject to continuing eligibility and renewal

mechanism.value: Removing immigration status as a formal eligibility barrier can convert legal inclusion into a usable health-care route when enrollment and provider access work

observations.method: California DHCS implementation FAQ and policy fact sheet.
observations.uncertainty: Policy availability does not establish successful enrollment, appointment access, treatment completion, affordability of non-covered needs, or improved health for every eligible resident.
observations.subgroup: Low-income California adults ages 26 through 49 who otherwise meet Medi-Cal eligibility requirements, including undocumented adults.
observations.counterinterpretation: Administrative, language, provider-capacity, transportation, and fear-related barriers can remain after a formal eligibility barrier is removed.

denominator.unit: nearly 100 undocumented adults in focus groups

enrollment.unit: percent of study participants who successfully enrolled in full-scope Medi-Cal

care_access.unit: percent of enrolled participants who had accessed health care at least once

experience.value: Participants generally reported positive access experiences and strong satisfaction with services

mechanism.value: The expansion reached beyond symbolic inclusion for many participants: enrollment was followed by at least one care encounter

observations.method: California Health Care Foundation qualitative focus-group study of nearly 100 undocumented immigrants newly eligible for full-scope Medi-Cal.
observations.uncertainty: The study is not a probability sample or longitudinal administrative evaluation; the figures cannot estimate statewide take-up, represent all undocumented adults, or establish health improvement or causal effects.
observations.subgroup: Previously ineligible adult undocumented immigrants who became eligible through the final phase of California's expansion.
observations.counterinterpretation: Participants who enrolled or participated in the study may differ from eligible adults who could not enroll, remained fearful, lacked providers, or disengaged after an initial visit.

new_enrollment.value: Adults without satisfactory immigration status who are 19 or older can no longer newly enroll in full-scope Medi-Cal

existing_members.value: Existing members can retain coverage if they renew on time and continue to meet Medi-Cal rules

mechanism.value: A system can move from broad formal inclusion to conditional continuity, making renewal timing, administrative legibility, and re-entry capacity part of practical security

observations.method: California DHCS public member guidance and immigrant-eligibility FAQ.
observations.uncertainty: The policy page describes eligibility rules, not observed disenrollment, delayed care, employment effects, household tradeoffs, or trust changes after the freeze.
observations.subgroup: Undocumented and other adults without satisfactory immigration status, with separate protections for children, pregnancy, and certain former foster youth.
observations.counterinterpretation: Existing coverage, emergency and pregnancy-related services, county assistance, and legal help may buffer some consequences; the size and distribution of that buffering remain open.

premium.unit: US dollars per month for specified full-coverage members ages 19 to 59

coverage_condition.value: Specified undocumented or unsatisfactory-status members must pay the monthly premium to keep full coverage

mechanism.value: Coverage can remain formally available while becoming contingent on recurring payment, creating a direct bridge from immigration status to household budget room and care continuity

observations.uncertainty: This is a future policy condition, not observed payment, disenrollment, forgone care, or health outcome data; actual incidence will depend on implementation and household resources.
observations.subgroup: Medi-Cal members ages 19 to 59 who are not pregnant and have undocumented or unsatisfactory immigration status and remain in full coverage.
observations.counterinterpretation: Premium exemptions, payment assistance, alternative county or safety-net routes, and changes in policy could alter realized effects.

observations.period: October 2023-March 2024 renewal determinations; procedural disenrollment follow-up

denominator.unit: people disenrolled from Medi-Cal for procedural reasons during the six-month survey period

procedural_disenrollment.unit: people disenrolled for procedural reasons during the survey period

measurement_route.value: DHCS used a follow-up survey to learn why people procedurally disenrolled, while explicitly warning that respondents may not represent the full disenrolled population

mechanism.value: Administrative continuity failures become visible through a feedback instrument, but the feedback route itself has contact, language, selection, and representativeness limits

observations.method: DHCS cumulative procedural-disenrollment survey report covering six months of renewal determinations.
observations.uncertainty: Survey respondents may not represent the full procedurally disenrolled population; the survey does not establish subsequent re-enrollment, care interruption, or health outcomes.
observations.subgroup: People procedurally disenrolled from Medi-Cal during the October 2023-March 2024 determination months; the survey excludes people found ineligible for other reasons or who requested discontinuance.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some procedural disenrollment may be temporary or corrected through later renewal, and some people may have other coverage; the reported count is not equivalent to a durable loss of care.

denominator.unit: days generally allowed to request a Medi-Cal fair hearing after receiving a Notice of Action

hearing_window.unit: days to request a fair hearing in the ordinary case

aid_pending.value: Benefits may continue pending review when the hearing is requested within the applicable 10-day protection window

correction_route.value: Members can discuss complaints with the county, file discrimination complaints, or request a hearing when benefits or services are denied or modified

mechanism.value: Formal correction exists as a time-bounded route from denial or modification to review, but its practical reach depends on notice, language, disability access, legal help, and successful follow-through

observations.uncertainty: The guidance establishes the route but does not measure hearing requests, reversal rates, wait times, member awareness, or whether correction restored care and trust.
observations.subgroup: Applicants and members whose Medi-Cal benefits or services were denied, modified, or handled in a way they contest.
observations.counterinterpretation: A formal hearing route can protect rights while remaining practically inaccessible to people facing language, disability, time, transportation, documentation, or fear barriers.

observations.period: July 2025-June 2026; member voice and attribution route

denominator.unit: members representing health-sector and lived-experience perspectives on the Voices and Vision Council

council_members.unit: members on the Voices and Vision Council

meeting_frequency.unit: quarterly meetings held by each advisory group during the reporting year

recommendation_route.value: Member recommendations were documented, voted on, posted with DHCS responses and progress updates, and used to shape communications planning; DHCS stated that implementation feasibility and next steps were still under review

communication_change.value: DHCS moved forward with a member-preferred plain-language text-message design after advisory testing

mechanism.value: Representation can become practical attribution when lived-experience input is connected to a documented recommendation, agency response, and visible communication change; this is influence evidence, not proof of improved coverage or health outcomes

observations.method: DHCS annual report on the Medi-Cal Member Advisory Committee and Voices and Vision Council.
observations.uncertainty: The report is an agency account of advisory process and early implementation; it does not establish population-wide representation, independent causal influence, or member-level outcome improvement.
observations.subgroup: Advisory members, including Medi-Cal members, caregivers, advocates, providers, health plans, and community partners; council composition is not equivalent to all Medi-Cal members.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal recommendations and one communication change can coexist with delayed implementation, limited agenda power, or continued barriers for people not represented in the advisory structures.

denominator.unit: calls placed to the Medi-Cal Managed Care Office of the Ombudsman across the first two quarters of reporting year 2025-2026

q1_calls_placed.unit: calls placed to the Ombudsman in January-March 2025 reporting months

q2_calls_placed.unit: calls placed to the Ombudsman in October-December 2025 reporting months

q1_abandoned.unit: calls abandoned before speaking to an Ombudsman analyst across January-March 2025

q2_abandoned.unit: calls abandoned before speaking to an Ombudsman analyst across October-December 2025

average_wait.unit: reported average monthly wait time across the two quarters

primary_route.value: Enrollment/disenrollment was the largest recorded contact result category, and many referrals went to county eligibility workers, managed care plans, or state hearings

mechanism.value: An Ombudsman makes correction operationally visible through contact volume, language, wait, abandonment, referral destination, and case-result fields; these measure route performance, not successful resolution or restored care

observations.method: DHCS SB 97 quarterly Ombudsman reports for 2025-2026 Q1 and Q2.
observations.uncertainty: The reports count contacts and recorded dispositions, not unique people, completed remedies, clinical outcomes, or whether a referral solved the member's problem; some tables suppress small cells and fee-for-service members are excluded from plan tables.
observations.subgroup: Medi-Cal managed-care members contacting the Ombudsman by phone or email; language, ethnicity, age, and plan fields are reported with different denominators and missingness.
observations.counterinterpretation: High contact volume can indicate strong awareness and reach of the correction route, unresolved system friction, or both; low abandonment does not prove low unmet need among people who never call.

denominator.unit: calls placed to the Medi-Cal Managed Care Office of the Ombudsman across April-June 2026

calls_placed.unit: calls placed to the Ombudsman across April-June 2026

abandoned_calls.unit: calls abandoned before speaking to an Ombudsman analyst across April-June 2026

average_wait.unit: minutes average monthly wait time in each month of April-June 2026

primary_issue.value: Access to care was about half of recorded primary issues in each month: 50.48% in April, 50.20% in May, and 50.31% in June

result_pattern.value: Enrollment/disenrollment remained the largest recorded contact result category, while referral accounted for about 22%-23%

mechanism.value: The correction route shows persistence rather than a one-time surge: queue friction is measurable, access-to-care demand remains dominant, and referral is still distinct from completed restoration

observations.method: DHCS SB 97 Quarter 4 2025-2026 Ombudsman report; monthly April-June 2026 tables were summed where appropriate.
observations.uncertainty: The report counts contacts and recorded dispositions, not unique people, completed remedies, clinical outcomes, or whether a referral solved the member's problem; denominator differences across tables and administrative coding remain important.
observations.subgroup: Medi-Cal managed-care members contacting the Ombudsman by phone or email during April-June 2026; the report's issue and result tables have different operational denominators.
observations.counterinterpretation: Persistent contact volume can reflect awareness and reach, unresolved friction, seasonal demand, or changes in reporting; stable wait and abandonment figures do not establish adequate access for members who never call.

related_sources.claim: Official enrollment fast facts include undocumented adults within the ACA expansion adult enrollment category.
Official enrollment and renewal data portal for later observed continuity checks.

boundary: This record follows a named state policy from formal eligibility through reported initial enrollment and care access, then into a later enrollment freeze and future premium condition. It does not establish statewide take-up, treatment completion, health improvement, employment continuity, household budget effects, verified remedy, or trust/action change.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official DHCS policy and enrollment pages and the CHCF study were reviewed for implementation scope, participant enrollment and care-use findings, later continuity rules, and measurement boundaries.
